source_text: Offeret arietem immaculatum sacerdoti. Christus aries; delictum nostrum portat. Sacerdos aestimat.
thought_title: The ram as Christ bearing our sin
orientation: Origen is interpreting the Levitical guilt offering, showing that the ram offered to the priest is a figure of Christ bearing our sin.
pass_a_gloss: He will offer an unblemished ram to the priest. Christ is the ram; he bears our sin. The priest assesses it.

choices.why: Keeps the ritual sense of the offering animal without moralizing it, matching the Levitical requirement.
Preserves the present tense and the singular 'delictum' as the collective sin borne by Christ.
Keeps the priest's judicial act of valuation distinct from mere seeing or judging.

pass_b_english: He will offer an unblemished ram to the priest (Leviticus 6:6). Christ is the ram; he bears our sin. The priest assesses it.

last_rejected.why: Source says 'our sin' is borne, but 'he' ambiguous: Christ or ram? Source has Christ as ram, one subject.
last_rejected.fix: Christ is the ram, bearing our sin. The priest assesses it.
last_rejected.ruling: Context 'Christus aries' makes 'he' unambiguous; pronoun agrees with Christ, the ram who bears sin.
